summary: V6.25.46 backend validation — 19/19 PASSED (8 new V6.25.46 + 3 V6.25.45 + 3 V6.25.43 + 5 V6.25.41 regression). All four real writer-tool surfaces (Atlas, Magic Architect, Manuscript, Outline/Beats) verified end-to-end. Coverage: atlas full pin lifecycle (PATCH map, POST new node pin, DELETE unpin keeps node), Pydantic confloat 0..1 validation rejects map_x>1.0 and <0 with 422, pin-existing-node path reuses node (location count unchanged), magic-system CRUD, manuscript chapter/scene/beat tree with strict parent-gating (chapter+parent → 400, scene without parent → 400, scene-under-scene → 400, beat-under-chapter → 400), PATCH body_md auto-recomputes word_count via whitespace tokenisation, cascading delete returns 3 (chapter + scene + beat) and tree returns total_word_count summed across sections. Permission model verified end-to-end: player registered fresh, accepted invite via /invites/{token}/accept, then GET /writer/atlas|magic|manuscript returns 200 with writable:false, POST returns 403 on all three surfaces. Reseed-checkpoint persistence verified live: db.reseed_checkpoints has 5 rows with {source_tag:'bible-v3', chunk_no, status:'ok', persisted_count, script_run_id}; db.nodes count for tag 'evereantha-bible-llm-seed-v3' = 64 mid-run (>0 as required). Background script PID 319 not touched. All regressions still green.
critical_code_review_comments: writer_tools.py — clean, well-bounded module (~383 lines), pydantic-validated inputs, every write path goes through _require_write/_can_write helpers. Admin bypass + GM-only writes correctly enforced.

writer_tools.py — _can_write does NOT honour any per-membership 'role' (e.g. an invited 'worldbuilder' player on someone else's table). The docstring (lines 22-25) calls this out as intentional ('they need a documented invite flow before they can edit'). Worth tracking as a future enhancement when membership-roles are introduced; not a bug today.

manuscript_patch — silently drops parent_id and kind on PATCH (lines 353-354). This is correct (immutable) but should ideally return 400 instead of silently ignoring; minor UX issue, not a regression.

atlas_create_pin existing-node branch — overwrites node.content with body.description when description is provided (line 151). Acceptable for an authoring tool but worth flagging: a re-pin operation will clobber the location's lore text if the caller supplies a description. Consider making content patch optional (only when explicitly requested).
manuscript_delete cascade — iterative BFS over parent_id; correct and bounded. No recursion-depth risk.
